title: AI and Authorship
answer: AI and authorship covers the questions of who or what counts as an author when a model contributes to a text, an image, a dataset or a piece of code, and how credit, accountability and originality are assigned in that arrangement. It sits inside research integrity and publishing ethics, where journals, universities, funders and standards bodies set the rules that working researchers then have to follow. The topic reaches beyond scholarly publishing into journalism, software, design and any setting where a produced work is attributed to a person or an organisation.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: AI and authorship covers the questions of who or what counts as an author when a model contributes to a text, an image, a dataset or a piece of code, and how credit, accountability and originality are assigned in that arrangement. It sits inside research integrity and publishing ethics, where journals, universities, funders and standards bodies set the rules that working researchers then have to follow. The topic reaches beyond scholarly publishing into journalism, software, design and any setting where a produced work is attributed to a person or an organisation.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The practical machinery is mostly editorial and administrative rather than computational: submission systems, authorship declaration forms, contributor role taxonomies, licence statements and disclosure fields that ask whether a generative tool was used and how. On the research side, provenance is carried by version control, model and prompt records, dataset documentation and logs that show what a system produced and what a human changed. Institutions tie these together through publication policies, integrity offices and repository metadata, so a claim about authorship can be traced back to a record rather than to memory.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Work in this area usually starts by separating two things that are often conflated: contribution, meaning what was actually done, and responsibility, meaning who answers for the finished output. Teams map contributions against established criteria for authorship, document tool use at the point it happens rather than at submission, and keep a written account of which passages, figures or analyses came from a model and which were produced or verified by a person. Reviewers and editors then apply journal or institutional policy to that record, and disputes are handled through the same correction and retraction routes used for other integrity problems.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The governing question is accountability: a model cannot consent, cannot hold a licence, cannot be contacted about an error and cannot be sanctioned, so responsibility has to rest with a named human or institution. Policies therefore tend to require disclosure of generative tool use, forbid listing a model as an author, and place the burden of accuracy, originality and rights clearance on the human authors. Copyright and licensing add a second layer, since the training data behind a model and the terms under which it was used affect whether an output can be published or reused, and plagiarism checks have to account for text that no person wrote. Provenance records, including model version, date and the extent of human editing, are what make these claims checkable after the fact.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Expect the rules to move from blanket bans and blanket permissions toward graded disclosure, where the level of detail required scales with how much a model shaped the work. Contributor taxonomies will likely be extended to record model involvement alongside human roles, and provenance standards will be folded into existing metadata rather than kept as a separate practice. Detection tools will remain unreliable enough that policy leans on declaration and audit instead of guessing, and the harder unresolved questions concern responsibility when a model's contribution is substantial but no human can reconstruct how it was reached.
